title: Is free will an illusion?
prompt: If every choice is the product of prior causes, in what sense are we free — and does the answer change how we should hold people responsible?

title: Would you enter Nozick's experience machine?
prompt: A machine can give you a lifetime of perfectly convincing pleasant experiences, indistinguishable from reality. Do you plug in? What does your answer say about what you actually value?

title: Does a just society require equality of outcome, or only opportunity?
prompt: Where should the line sit between fairness of starting points and fairness of results — and who gets to draw it?

title: Is it ever rational to act against your own self-interest?
prompt: Duty, love, principle — can these give you real reasons that outrank your own good, or are they self-interest in disguise?

title: Should the state be neutral about how people should live?
prompt: Liberalism says the state shouldn't pick a vision of the good life. Is genuine neutrality possible — or even desirable?

title: Do we have duties to future generations?
prompt: People who don't yet exist can't consent or complain. Do we still owe them a habitable world, and how much are we obliged to sacrifice now?

title: Is patriotism a virtue or a bias?
prompt: Loving your country over others: a healthy loyalty, or an arbitrary accident of birth dressed up as morality?

title: Can a war ever be just?
prompt: Under what conditions, if any, is organised killing morally permissible — and do modern wars ever actually meet them?

title: Is there a meaningful difference between killing and letting die?
prompt: The trolley problem in one line: is pulling the lever morally different from refusing to? Why should intention or action matter more than the body count?

title: Does moral truth exist, or do we invent it?
prompt: Are 'torturing for fun is wrong' and 'the earth orbits the sun' the same kind of fact — or is one just a very strong feeling we share?

title: Should freedom of speech protect speech you find abhorrent?
prompt: Where, if anywhere, is the principled line between protected expression and harm — and who can be trusted to enforce it?

title: Is democracy the best system, or just the least bad one?
prompt: If most people are wrong about most things, why should majority preference decide anything? What would a better system even look like?

title: Can you be moral without believing in objective morality?
prompt: If morality is ultimately human-made, does 'because it's wrong' still carry any weight — or does everything become permitted?

title: How much inequality can a healthy society tolerate?
prompt: Some gap seems to drive effort and innovation; too large a gap seems to corrode trust and legitimacy. Where's the tipping point?

title: Is a life of comfort a life well lived?
prompt: Would you trade a peaceful, pleasant existence for a harder one that meant more? Is struggle part of a good life, or just a cost of a bad one?

title: Do borders have any moral justification?
prompt: Is a nation entitled to decide who may enter and belong — or is the accident of where you were born just the last great unearned privilege?

title: Should we trust experts over our own judgement?
prompt: Deferring to specialists is efficient but disempowering; thinking for yourself is empowering but often wrong. How do you decide when to defer?

title: Is nationalism the disease or the cure of the modern age?
prompt: A source of solidarity and self-government, or of division and war? Can you have the belonging without the hostility?

title: What, if anything, do we owe to strangers on the other side of the world?
prompt: If a child drowning in front of you demands rescue, why does distance weaken the obligation to one dying of preventable causes abroad?

title: Is technological progress the same as human progress?
prompt: We are richer and more capable than any ancestors — are we wiser, freer, or happier? What would count as evidence either way?

title: Can power ever be truly legitimate?
prompt: Consent, tradition, results, force — every basis for authority has a crack in it. Is legitimacy real, or a story the powerful tell?

title: Should you be free to sell anything you own, including your body and choices?
prompt: Markets in kidneys, votes, or labour hours: where should the line be between a free exchange and an exploitative one?
